quote.description: Verbatim words from the source, checked against the cited paragraph.

ref_capabilities.description: Capability-map matches: which capability each element touches.

capability_id.description: The map's own id, e.g. KNW.11 (technology) or B1.1.2 (business).

confidence.description: How sure the match is, in the matcher's own words.

element_id.description: The model element this is about. Empty only when status=missing.

map.description: The capability map's artifact id in the reference corpus.

map_version.description: The pinned version the match was made against.

ref_concepts.description: The element linked to a fabric vocabulary concept.

concept_iri.description: Absent for a candidate the vocabulary does not hold yet.

confidence.description: How sure the match is, in the matcher's own words.

element_id.description: The model element this reference is about.

ref_realisations.description: Realisation-map entries: what realises each matched capability.

catalogue_id.description: The reference-architecture catalogue id (cmp-...) when the realiser is a catalogue component.

confidence.description: How sure the match is, in the matcher's own words.

element_id.description: The model element this reference is about.

realised_by.description: What realises the capability: a product, platform or existing system.

ref_repository.description: The element resolved against the EA repository (through the EA port's ea_search). Drives create-vs-update at import and the impact view.

candidates.description: The other repository objects considered, for the architect to pick from.

confidence.description: How sure the match is, in the matcher's own words.

element_id.description: The model element this reference is about.

repository_class.description: The repository's own class name for the object.

review_decision.description: One architect decision at the modelling gate (D8), per element or relation.

actor.description: The signed-in human. Blank is refused.

correction.description: With state=corrected: the fields that change.

aliases.description: Other names for the same artifact.

status.description: The change vocabulary plus missing = needed, and nothing realises it.

description: What modelling emits: the FR-11 engine spec UNCHANGED under `spec`, with provenance, sources, references, change status, renames, reviews, open questions and refused relations beside it (ADR docs/decisions/2026-10-24-architecture-modelling.md). Generated from lab.core.modelling; never edit by hand.

changes.description: Per element, its change relative to the EA repository, for impact views (as-is = consumed, updated, removed; to-be = consumed, updated, new). The lab's visualisation does not read it yet.

dropped.description: Relations proposed but refused (illegal by the matrix, an undeclared or ambiguous endpoint), each with its reason.

gaps.description: Joins a mapper could not make.

references.description: What each model element is in other registers.

renamed_from.description: Element id -> the ids it had in earlier runs, declared only on evidence (same provenance location or the same repository id).

reviews.description: Architect decisions at the modelling gate, carried across re-runs: kept on an id that still exists, moved across a rename (an element's, or a relation endpoint's), and raised as `review-orphaned` when the id is gone.

x-agent.prompt:
# Model the architecture the inputs describe

You are an enterprise architect. You are given one or more INPUTS, each under a key (S1, S2, ...):
documents as text with numbered paragraphs (`[¶n]`), and possibly images, figures or diagrams.
Build the ArchiMate 3.1 model those inputs describe, and cite, for every element and every
relationship, the words in the inputs that justify it.

## What to model

Model every layer the inputs actually describe. Do not fill a layer the inputs are silent about.
- **Motivation**: drivers, goals, outcomes, principles, requirements, constraints and stakeholders the
  inputs state.
- **Strategy**: capabilities, value streams, resources and courses of action the inputs name.
- **Business**: actors and roles, business processes, functions, events and services, and business
  objects. Decompose behaviour where the ACTION changes: retrieving is not interpreting, and
  interpreting is not deciding. Name functions verb plus object ("assess referral").
- **Data**: data objects, and which business object each realises.
- **Application**: the application components, interfaces, services and functions the inputs
  describe, including existing systems by their own names.
- **Technology**: nodes, system software, devices, technology services and networks the inputs
  describe.

An element the inputs only imply is not invented. If it is plainly part of this system, include it
and cite the words that imply it. Otherwise, ask about it in `openQuestions`.

## Reading the inputs

- Read every input fully before classifying anything.
- A specific product, stencil or icon (a database cylinder, a server, a cloud glyph) is strong
  evidence of type and layer. A plain box, a colour or a container is weak evidence: decide from the
  caption and from what connects to it.
- An interface is an access point: the owner is composed of it, and it is assigned to the service
  reached through it.
- A box drawn around others is usually a boundary (a system, a node, a domain), not an element.
- Requirements are evidence about the system, not a second system.
- Where two inputs disagree, keep both readings out of the model and ask in `openQuestions`,
  quoting both sides.

## Relationships

Every relationship has a direction: server to served, whole to part, realiser to realised, performer
to behaviour, behaviour to the object it accesses. Name both ends by an element's exact `name`. Use
`accessType` only on an Access relationship. Use only relationships ArchiMate permits between the two
types; a relationship it forbids is discarded downstream, not repaired.

## Citations

Every element and every relationship cites at least one source:
- `source`: the input's key, exactly as shown (S1).
- `location`: where in it, as `{"paragraph": n}` (the `[¶n]` number), `{"page": n}`,
  `{"figure": n}` or `{"shape": "<id>"}`.
- `quote`: the input's OWN words, copied exactly, short enough to be the evidence and nothing more.
  Never quote the `[¶n]` marker. Never paraphrase: a paraphrase is not evidence, and it is checked.
  For a figure or a diagram, quote the label or caption as you read it.

If you cannot cite an element, it does not belong in the model. Raise it in `openQuestions`.

## Naming

Use the inputs' own name for each element. One element per thing: if two names describe the same
thing, choose one and cite both passages. A name is unique across the whole model: if the inputs use
one word for two things (a "Referral" object and a "Referral" process), name them apart ("Referral",
"Handle referral"), because relationships name their ends by name.

## How to answer

Return ONE JSON object matching the schema and nothing else: no prose before it, no markdown fence,
no explanation after it. The reply is parsed, and anything around the object is a parse failure.
It has five fields: `systemName` (what the inputs call the system), `summary` (two or three
sentences), `elements`, `relationships` and `openQuestions`.

Where you do not know something, say so in `openQuestions` rather than inventing a plausible value.
A fabricated element is indistinguishable from a real one downstream, which is the one failure this
model cannot recover from.

location.description: Where in that input: the [¶n] paragraph number, a page, a figure number or a diagram shape id.

quote.description: The input's OWN words that justify this item, copied exactly. For a figure or diagram, the label or caption as read.

source.description: The key of the input this came from, as shown (S1, S2, ...).

name.description: The element's name, as the input names it. Unique across the model.

role.description: What it is and does in this system, in plain language.

type.description: The exact ArchiMate 3.1 type. Its layer and aspect follow from it.

elements.description: Names of the elements the question is about.

schema.title: Architecture model drawn from the inputs

x-id-rule: Every element and relation id matches [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ (an IRI local name). An element id is a prefix for its type plus a slug of its name, so a re-run that keeps the name keeps the id. The prefix is x-id-prefixes' for the type, otherwise the type's own name in kebab case (SystemSoftware -> 'system-software-'). A name with nothing to slug (e.g. wholly Arabic) gets 'h' plus a hash of the name. A rename is a new id, declared in `renamed_from` when modelling can show it is the same thing. A relation id is 'r-' + md5(src|type|tgt)[:10].
